bull.b: Sustained positive free cash flow (~$1.17B TTM) provides durable funding for R&D, AI investments, buybacks and working capital without relying solely on equity raises. Strong cash conversion versus GAAP losses improves financial optionality and reduces near-term refinancing risk.

bull.t: High net revenue retention and large-account expansion
bull.b: 126% net revenue retention and accelerating large-account counts indicate sticky, expanding consumption from existing customers. Land-and-expand dynamics in a usage-based model create durable recurring revenue growth and lower marginal sales costs per account over time.

bull.t: Strategic cloud and AI partnerships broaden reach
bull.b: Material partnerships (large AWS deal, OpenAI tie-up, SAP integration) strengthen distribution, lower infrastructure cost headwinds, and accelerate enterprise AI workload adoption. These partnerships deepen platform integration and widen competitive moats over the medium term.

bear.b: Debt-to-equity rising above 1x marks a structural shift toward a more leveraged capital structure. With ongoing GAAP losses, higher leverage increases fixed obligations, constrains flexibility for opportunistic investments, and raises refinancing and covenant sensitivity over the next several quarters.

bear.t: Persistent GAAP losses and negative returns
bear.b: Meaningful negative net margins and deeply negative ROE reflect ongoing GAAP unprofitability despite gross margin strength. Persistent accounting losses limit retained earnings, weaken equity cushions and may require sustained cash generation to fund growth until GAAP break-even is achieved.

Rapid scaling of lower-margin AI workloads can structurally compress blended gross margins unless cloud-cost offsets or price realization keep pace. Additionally, customers may throttle usage for cost control, which could cap consumption growth and pressure long-term revenue per account.
